state.purpose: Can is a programming language for AI coding agents. Correctness, stable contracts and observable product behavior outrank every other goal; total tokens per successful agent task is a secondary measured outcome, not a primary acceptance claim. The 24 September 2026 implementation task list T01-T27 is a plan, not a statement that any production change has shipped. There are zero external users and no compatibility requirements for old syntax, ABI, spellings, generated TypeScript layouts or goldens. Generated TypeScript must lower equivalent Can operations to native JavaScript/Bun operations, adding only adapters that preserve Can contracts and immutability. Gates 1-5 require linked reproducible evidence; no language mechanism is credited by a pilot. Select implementation judgments on this evidence without asking the user.
state.task_graph: T01 freezes a dated baseline and repeatable harness: supported Bun/compiler versions, disposable build directories, core regression commands, exact current-vs-new diagnostic fixtures, and a fixture registry with creation/refactor/repair prompts, held-out variants, hidden checks and model/effort settings under the evaluation protocol. After T01, T02/T03/T06/T07/T18/T19 may proceed in parallel. T03 unlocks T04/T05/T08; T05 and T06 unlock T10; T03/T05/T06/T07 unlock T21. T10 unlocks T11/T12/T13; T21 unlocks T22. T09 integrates T02-T08 across compiler, runtime metadata, package graph, formatter, CLI diagnostics, docs and examples, runs full regression plus cross-feature negatives (owner record through generic/package boundary, variant leaf across imports, fixture link after alias rename, error report after lineage change), regenerates outputs once from integrated source, and completes Gate 1/2 core integration only when reproducible; T09 precedes T16 while invoice and browser lanes continue on their stated prerequisites. T10 adds source action declarations with checked catalogue symbols using the exact-path parser/type contract, with the selected captured paths as the public invoice declarations and no compatibility route. T14 builds invoice protected read/write operations with three thin action handlers against a real disposable database. T17 runs the complete server matrix for Gate 3; T19 pins official Bun 1.4.2 Linux x64 on Debian 13 amd64/glibc; T20 qualifies Gate 4 server SaaS on the installed Linux artifact. T21 implements canlc build --target browser as a distinct main-thread root/profile with transitive capability closure and a compiler-produced content-addressed same-origin asset. T26 updates docs and runs held-out agent comparisons; T27 performs the final release audit. Never merge two workers' compiler or catalogue edits blindly; integrate against one locked revision and rerun affected checks.
state.evidence_limits: Only bounded disposable probes exist. A two-package owner probe passed 11 assertion roots showing constructor, with, JSON decode, assertion-input and supplied-completion bypasses of rejecting factories. A nested-pattern probe ran 13 cases where final decliend and nested paidd silently bind and identical paid text tests a leaf under payment but binds under int. A 16-case variant matrix passed 12 builds with 24 assertions and 4 expected checker rejections, showing path-sensitive direct rejection with bridge/leaf admission. A generic-helper probe passed 28/28 assertions with disjoint singleton failure domains. A 12-check FormData probe showed equal-length parallel arrays misassociating cross-row values. Route-capture work carries 82 trial assertions on pinned Bun with strict 400/404/405 boundaries. An HTMX probe observed a real 503 fragment arriving over HTTP yet leaving stale 422 feedback visible. An 18-assertion invoice slice passed without any live database, HTTP response or DOM. No live production invoice flow, webhook ledger, browser grid, or Linux install qualification has passed. No held-out agent creation/refactor/repair comparison has run; whole-task token effects are unmeasured. Jev probabilities and confidence values are advisory only, not acceptance proof, and these calls run no Can code and establish no calibration.
state.fixed_constraints: Every compiler or catalogue change must add positive, negative and diagnostic-span tests plus regenerated TypeScript and goldens as applicable. Every edit to authored runtime/ or tools/runtime/ TypeScript must run bun run lint:fix:runtime, bun run format:runtime, bun run check:runtime and the relevant tests, using bun run lint:runtime --format=agent for compact diagnostics. Never hand-edit generated runtime/catalogue.ts or pinned vendor files. Observable product tests must inspect native HTTP, browser and database results, not merely a Can assertion or Jev advice. Each qualification report must record the actual model and version, compiler revision, environment and failures. Deferred mechanisms stay out of the build: DI-03 finite error-set parameters, DI-08 capture-binding syntax, DI-14a mutation RETURNING, DI-17 new native AI wrapper/batch/callable forms, DI-18 static escape/consumed-fault additions, DI-19 unrestricted SDK imports, DI-20 bulk immutable collections, DI-22 named-field constructors and DI-23 multiline grammar. Workers must not invent them to make a test pass.

integration_strategy.instructions: Which core-integration strategy should T09 enforce for T02-T08, balancing reproducible contracts against parallel invoice, browser and webhook progress? Do not claim measured token savings.

criteria.single_locked_integration: Integrate T02-T08 against one locked revision across compiler, runtime metadata, package graph, formatter, CLI diagnostics, docs and examples. Run full regression plus cross-feature negatives covering an owner record through a generic/package boundary, a variant leaf across imports, a fixture link after an alias rename, and an error report after a lineage change. Regenerate outputs once from the integrated source and record any intended source break. Gate 1/2 passes only on reproducible results; T16 waits on T09 while invoice and browser lanes advance on their own prerequisites.
criteria.per_lane_incremental: Let each core lane land and regenerate its own goldens independently, merging opportunistically and postponing cross-feature negatives until invoice or browser qualification exposes a conflict.
criteria.block_all_on_core: Freeze every invoice, browser, webhook and shutdown branch until T09 fully passes, permitting no parallel lane work even where the graph names an earlier prerequisite as sufficient.

replay_ledger.instructions: Which grid-write uncertainty contract should T14 implement for invoice mutations, given lost acknowledgements, foreign/nonexistent access, and HTML/JSON case mapping? Judge disclosure, idempotency and reconciliation clarity.

criteria.same_transaction_ledger: Store a durable actor, invoice, operation_id and canonical-request-digest entry with the committed response in the same database transaction as the invoice mutation. A same-ID same-digest replay returns the prior result with no second effect; same ID with a different digest is a conflict. Foreign and nonexistent invoices share one nondisclosing 403 after authentication; malformed captures fail 400 before protected entry. Map validation to five HTML and five JSON save cases plus three typed GET load cases, enforcing the 8192-byte JSON POST cap and the 2048-byte/64-row HTML form caps. The HTML client rereads after uncertainty; the grid keeps its identified attempt and either retries the identical payload and ID or performs an authorized read. Bounded retention preserves the reconciliation path; renderer failure after commit may surface 500 with uncertain state.
criteria.separate_ledger_transaction: Commit the invoice mutation first, then persist the replay/outbox record in a later transaction with background reconciliation, accepting a window where the row changed but the ledger entry is absent.
criteria.client_new_id_retry: After any 503, dropped connection, abort or disposal, have the browser mint a fresh operation_id for each retry, with the server treating every new ID as a distinct mutation that may duplicate the business effect.

browser_closure.instructions: Which browser build boundary should T21/T22 enforce for the Can-authored grid, given shared wire contracts, server secrets, and DOM/Fetch safety? Judge least privilege and verifiability.

criteria.strict_transitive_closure: Build canlc build --target browser as a distinct main-thread root and profile with a compiler-checked transitive browser capability closure over callable and generic paths. Exclude SQL, process, files, secrets and server crypto, audit emitted imports and sourcemaps, share locked pure packages and strict wire codecs, and test Bun/browser int64, finite floats, variants, option, duplicate/unknown fields and owner wire boundaries in named browsers. Use opaque app/view/node/state handles, safe native DOM/text/attributes/focus, event snapshots, view-scoped listener/timer disposal and versioned immutable replacement. The asset is compiler-produced, content-addressed and same-origin. No arbitrary authored JS/TS or worker profile is admitted; Fetch abort is local cancellation only, never proof of server rollback.
criteria.runtime_guarded_shared: Use one shared build profile for Bun and browser, bundle server-capable imports, and rely on runtime checks at each call site to refuse SQL, process, file, secret or server-crypto use when running in the browser.
criteria.permissive_bundling: Admit arbitrary authored JS/TS, inline scripts, third-party browser bundles and a worker profile alongside compiler output, without a content-addressed same-origin restriction or capability audit.
